result.note: Tests the labour code consolidation, labour's place in the Concurrent List and the Delhi High Court proceedings on Industrial Relations Code rules.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's labour codes, as reported in February 2026:
items: Since 2019, 29 labour laws have been folded into four labour codes.
Labour is a subject in the Union List of the Constitution.
While the Centre writes the codes, states write their own rules under them.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because labour sits on the Concurrent List, not the Union List. Because states frame their own rules, the rollout of the codes is expected to be uneven, especially early on.
questions.source: Labour sits on the Concurrent List.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the Centre told which court that it would finalise the remaining rules to operationalise parts of the Industrial Relations Code by end-February 2026?
questions.explain: The Centre gave the undertaking to the Delhi High Court. Petitioners there argued the Code was in force but lacked rules on how labour courts or industrial tribunals operate and how members are appointed.
questions.source: On Monday, the Centre told the Delhi High Court it will finalise the remaining rules to operationalise parts of the Industrial Relations Code by end-February, after petitioners warned the system was running without an instruction book.
